A Forest Business School Short Course

Project Flow
in Forestry

Forestry professionals who finish projects on time earn more, build stronger reputations, and take on more work. This four-session short course gives you the framework to make that happen — consistently.

4 Live Sessions
90 Min. Each
11 SAF CFE Credits
Express Your Interest About the Course

The Problem

Projects in forestry almost always
run longer than they should.

You know the pattern: the landing sits longer than expected, the timber degrades, the mill waits, the landowner is frustrated, the contract stretches past two years. Every delay has a cost — and most of those delays are preventable.

Idle Iron

Equipment payments don't pause when machines are waiting on wood. Delays in the woods starve the mill and burn margin you never recover.

Timber Degrade

High-value timber stains and loses grade on the landing. Time kills value the moment a tree comes down.

Reputation on the Line

Landowners and mills remember projects that drag. Foresters who finish on time — or early — become the people everyone wants to work with.

Revenue Left Behind

Finishing one project on time means starting the next one sooner. Consistent project tempo compounds into real money over a career.

What Changes

When you manage flow,
the work takes care of itself.

Critical Chain Project Management is a proven framework for finishing projects faster — not by working harder, but by working in the right order, protecting the right tasks, and eliminating the habits that quietly kill every timeline.

01

You finish on time — or early

Not by accident. By design. CCPM gives you a system for identifying and protecting the tasks that actually determine when a project ends.

02

Your reputation compounds

Contractors, landowners, and agencies remember who delivers. Being the professional who finishes well is a competitive advantage that builds over time.

03

You become a linchpin

The professional who keeps projects moving — who others depend on to clear the path — is indispensable. That's the position CCPM helps you earn.

04

You stop fighting the same fires

Bad multitasking, procrastination, task dependency, and scope creep are diagnosable and treatable. This course names them and shows you how to fix them.

The Course

Four sessions.
One month. Real work applied.

Each 90-minute live session is built around discussion, case studies drawn from real forestry operations, and direct application to your own projects. Sessions are spaced one week apart — intentionally — to give you time to test ideas between meetings.

Session 01

Project Flow & Tempo

Why projects run long. The five diseases that kill every timeline. Why finishing early matters more than you think — and how to start thinking about it differently.

Session 02

CCPM Explained

The Theory of Constraints and the Critical Chain. How to identify the sequence of tasks that actually determines when your project ends. Buffers, dependencies, and the 50% rule.

Session 03

Goldratt's Rules of Flow

Eight rules that keep a project moving — applied to real forestry operations. Kit ready, work steady. Manage flow and the work will go.

Session 04

Adopting the Mindset

Implementing CCPM and overcoming resistance to change. Case studies. Your own CCPM action plan for a project you're working on right now.

Remote delivery. All sessions are held live via video conference. Sessions are recorded for participants who occasionally need to miss one. The course is delivered over approximately one month.

The Framework

Eight rules.
All actionable tomorrow.

The Rules of Flow are practical heuristics drawn from Goldratt's work and applied to real forestry operations across the Northeast.

Rule 1

Multi-Tasks Hold Others Back

Stop juggling. Finish what others are waiting for first.

Rule 2

Kit Ready, Work Steady

Don't start without permits, layout, and markets lined up.

Rule 3

Step Back & Find Cracks

Triage your priorities before they triage you.

Rule 4

Manage Flow, Work Will Go

Synchronize tasks, people, and iron. Flow management is the job.

Rule 5

Outcome Poor? Alter Core

Apply the right resource to break the constraint. Use a longer lever.

Rule 6

Seek & Tweak

Fix the root cause, not just the symptom. Stop redoing the same work.

Rule 7

Stacks, Not Hacks

Systems are faster than ad hoc fixes. Standardize the routine.

Rule 8

Goals, Not Roles

Abolish local optimization. Protect the global goal of the project.

Who It's For

If you manage work in the woods,
this course is for you.

The Course Text

Timber Tempo

Project Flow in Forestry — by Steven Bick

The course is built around Timber Tempo, a book that introduces Critical Chain Project Management to the forestry and forest products world through vivid case stories — from sawmill operations and timber procurement to land management and agency work.

Enrolled participants receive a free copy of the audiobook. The book is available in print and Kindle editions through Amazon.

The Instructor

Dr. Steven Bick, CF

Director, The Forest Business School  ·  Principal, Northeast Forests LLC  ·  Moretown, VT

Steve Bick is a consulting forester, educator, and the founder of Northeast Forests LLC. He has more than thirty years of experience providing professional development for working landscape professionals across the Northeast and beyond.

He is the author or co-author of ten books on forestry and conservation topics, including Timber Tempo, the text at the center of this course, and is the director of the Forest Business School.
